newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end lower on a strong yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end lower on a strong yen.

text.p: Yen-denominated gold futures ended lower across the board on Thursday, pressured by the yen's firmer tone against the dollar, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from five to 13 yen per gram lower. Benchmark August was down five at 1,337 yen.
Gold futures market reacted little to news that the International Monetary Fund (IMF) did not reach a decision on gold sales on Wednesday.
"Private investors' attention was more on the currency market than on the IMF's gold sales plan," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
Spot gold was quoted at $383.10/383.50 per ounce at 0725 GMT, against $383.05/383.55 in New York on Wednesday.
Spot gold was marked down in early morning trade, weighed down by selling from overseas investors, but buying by Japanese trade houses helped gold recover from early lows.
Private investors built fresh long positions, particularly in distant months, while trade houses sold futures while buying spot gold in arbitrage trade, the traders said.
One trader said gold will remain confined within a trading range between $382.5 and $384.00 in the near term.
Silver and palladium futures were weaker in tandem with gold, while platinum futures ended mixed.

August and December contracts of palladium futures hit their life-of-contract lows in continued bearish sentiment, while views that platinum were oversold, helped private investors hunting for bargains in platinum futures, they said.
Benchmark August silver ended flat at 181.2 yen. Benchmark August platinum was down one yen at 1,363 yen.
Benchmark August palladium was down two yen at 428 yen.
